title: Pay Cycles — Dynamic Take-Home Budgeting QA
testingOrder: Start with Section 1 to reach the feature. Create cycles in Section 3, then test the import in Section 4. Sections 6 (mobile) and 7 (permissions/deletion) can be run last.

groups.name: Consolidated menu
items: Budget page toolbar shows only two buttons: 'Import Budget' (primary) and 'Manage ▾' (secondary) — no separate 'Budget Template' button
'Import from Template' has been renamed to 'Import Budget'
Click 'Manage ▾' → dropdown opens below the button with a rotating chevron and two items: 'Budget Template' and 'Pay Cycles'
Click outside the open menu → it closes
Press Escape with the menu open → it closes
Manage → Budget Template opens the existing Budget Template modal (Template + Recurring tabs)
Manage → Pay Cycles opens the Pay Cycles modal

groups.name: List view
items: Empty state shows 'No pay cycles yet' with an '+ Add Pay Cycle' button
Existing cycles are grouped by earner (owner display name), 'Unassigned' group for cycles with no owner
Each cycle row shows label, frequency badge, target income category, and a schedule summary (amount/check, extra months for biweekly/weekly)
Inactive cycles show an '(inactive)' marker

groups.name: Add / edit form
items: Frequency = Weekly or Biweekly → shows an 'Anchor date' field (no day-of-month fields)
Frequency = Semi-monthly → shows two day-of-month pickers, each with a 'Last day of month' option
Frequency = Monthly → shows one day-of-month picker with a 'Last day of month' option
Income category select lists only income categories (default 'Take Home Pay')
Earner select lists household members plus a '— Household —' (unassigned) option
Per-paycheck amount uses the currency input (formats on blur)
Optional Starts / Ends (effective range) date fields are present
Active checkbox toggles whether the cycle is included in projections
Saving with an empty label → inline error 'Label is required'
Saving weekly/biweekly with no anchor date → inline error about anchor date
Saving amount 0 → inline error 'must be greater than 0'
Successful save → toast, returns to list, new/edited cycle appears
Delete uses the two-click confirm button; deleting removes the cycle with a toast

groups.name: Biweekly
items: Biweekly, anchor 2026-01-02, $1,750 → preview says 26 paychecks/yr, $45,500/yr, extra in Jan & Jul
Change the anchor to a mid-year date (e.g. 2026-06-15) → the preview stays populated for ALL months (Jan–May are NOT blank), still 26 checks
The per-month bars highlight the two 3-paycheck months in the warning color

groups.name: Weekly / Semi-monthly / Monthly
items: Weekly, anchor 2026-01-02, $875 → 52 paychecks/yr, extra (5-check) months Jan/May/Jul/Oct
Semi-monthly (15th & Last day) → 24 paychecks/yr, 'Same number of paychecks every month'
Monthly (day 31) → 12 paychecks/yr; a monthly on the 31st still lands in February (clamped to the 28th)
Clearing the anchor for weekly/biweekly → preview says 'Enter an anchor date to preview the schedule'

groups.name: Wizard flow
items: Import Budget wizard now has 4 steps: Template → Recurring → Expected Income → Review
Step 3 'Expected Income' shows one row per income category with the summed projected take-home
Each row shows a per-earner breakdown (e.g. 'Robert (ABC Fitness) 3×$1,750 = $5,250 · Sarah … ')
A 3-paycheck month shows an '⚡ extra check' marker on the affected category
Amounts are editable; unchecking a row excludes it (row dims)
If a category already has a budget value, a skip/overwrite/add conflict select appears with the existing amount
No cycles configured → empty state with a 'Set up pay cycles →' link that opens the Pay Cycles modal
Review (step 4) lists included pay-cycle income under 'Expected Income (Pay Cycles)' and counts it in the summary

groups.name: Applied result
items: Apply a NORMAL month → Take Home Pay budget = sum of 2×each biweekly earner
Apply a 3-PAYCHECK month → Take Home Pay budget is higher by exactly one extra check
Budgeted Income KPI and the Income section reflect the imported value (stored positive)
Re-import the same month with default (Overwrite) → income budget is unchanged (no doubling)
Set a row's conflict action to 'Add to it' → re-import adds to the existing value
Collision: if the template and a pay cycle both target Take Home Pay, the review step shows a warning; pay cycles win (applied last)

groups.name: Edge cases
items: A cycle with an effective_end before the imported month → does not appear in Expected Income
An inactive cycle → does not appear in Expected Income
Two cycles targeting the same income category → summed into one row with both in the breakdown
Two earners with different anchors → their extra-paycheck months differ and each is reflected in the right month

groups.name: Permissions
items: Member WITHOUT budgets.edit → 'Manage' menu trigger and 'Import Budget' are disabled (faded, non-interactive)
Member WITH budgets.edit → can open the menu, manage pay cycles, and import

groups.name: Responsive
items: Mobile budget toolbar shows 'Import Budget' and 'Manage' as two full-width buttons
Tapping 'Manage' opens a bottom sheet listing Budget Template and Pay Cycles (icon + label + description)
Pay Cycles modal and the import wizard render as bottom sheets on mobile
Touch targets are at least 44px; the form is usable without the keyboard covering fields

groups.name: Dependency handling
items: Delete-preview for a user who owns pay cycles lists 'N pay cycle(s) will be unassigned (kept in budget projections)'
After permanent deletion, the owned cycles remain but show under the 'Unassigned' group (owner cleared)
The unassigned cycles still contribute to the import projection
